llm_calls.reasoning: The alert shows checkout failing about 36% of requests on a fast burn, with no other open incidents. Checkout depends on many services, so the root cause may be a downstream dependency, a recent change, or a flag. I am giving each investigator a starting question.
Start broad: checkout error ratio and requests trend, plus checkout's client-span error rates per dependency. Run in parallel.

Step 1 shows checkout server error ratio ~0.48 and rising, while frontend and frontend-proxy are only ~0.03. Checkout's client spans show CartService/GetCart with STATUS_CODE_ERROR (~0.12), and CurrencyService/Convert and ProductCatalog/GetProduct with elevated non-error values. Next I'll compare each dependency's own server-side error rate and latency, and trend checkout's client-side errors by span over time, to see which dependency is actually failing.

Step 2 narrowed the failure to checkout's client calls to CartService/GetCart, which return STATUS_CODE_ERROR and rise from 0.03 to 0.13 over the hour. The other dependencies show only low latency and no client errors, and the per-service SLI selector for dependencies returned nothing. Next I'll check cart's own server-side errors by span, the error ratio across all services to confirm which are unhealthy, and cart's server error trend to see whether cart itself is failing or only as seen from checkout.

Checkout's client GetCart errors rise from 0.03 to 0.13/s, but cart's server spans show no STATUS_CODE_ERROR, and cart's p95 is about 2ms. That points to a failure seen only from checkout's side. Next I'll compare checkout's client GetCart latency and call volume against cart's server GetCart latency and status.

Checkout's client GetCart errors rise while cart's server spans show no errors and steady ~1.9ms p95, so the failure looks local to checkout or its path to cart. Cart's GetCart server call rate climbs to about 1.1/s, far above checkout's own GetCart rate of about 0.2/s, so other callers may be involved. Next I'll check checkout restarts and memory, and the call rate split by span_kind for cart.

Checkout's server error ratio is about 0.48-0.54 and rising. Its client GetCart errors are rising, but cart's own server spans show no errors and about 1.9 ms p95, so the fault looks local to checkout or its path to cart. Checkout's memory shows a new pod (checkout-6b7fbd6cdc-lj2vj) appearing around 19:23:53, which suggests a rollout at that time. Next I'll pin the pod and ReplicaSet start times, and check whether frontend's calls to cart are erroring too.

Checkout's own server error ratio is about 0.48 to 0.54 and rising since about 19:24. The error comes from checkout's client calls to CartService/GetCart, while cart's server spans show no errors and a steady p95 of about 1.9 ms, so the failure looks local to checkout or its path to cart. A second checkout pod appeared around 19:23:53, which may point to a rollout, so next I'll check the pod and ReplicaSet creation times and checkout's PlaceOrder latency.

Metrics show checkout's server error ratio climbing fast from about 0.18 to 0.54 starting around 19:24, while the only failing client span is checkout's CartService/GetCart. Cart's own server spans show no errors and a steady p95 near 1.9 ms, so the failure is visible only from checkout's side. I did not get rollout, pod-creation, or log data, so the cause inside checkout or on its path to cart is still open.

Starting with the brief: pull checkout error logs from Loki and error traces from Jaeger in parallel. Checkout's own logs and traces should show which dependency's exception surfaces on failing child spans.

Checkout's error traces (ev_ca3fefb3716edacf) show 20 GetCart client spans failing with "dial tcp 10.96.20.113:9999: i/o timeout", and checkout's own error logs are empty (ev_756b10024bf0b8c2). Cart looks like the failing dependency, so next I'll check cart's logs and error traces, and open one error trace in full.

Checkout's own error logs are empty, but its error traces show every failing GetCart call dialing 10.96.20.113:9999 with an i/o timeout, and cart's logs contain only info lines. Next I'll read checkout's logs mentioning cart for the address or connection setup, check whether cart's GetCart server spans record errors, and look for cart warnings.

Checkout's failing GetCart client spans all dial cart:9999 (10.96.20.113) and time out, while cart's own logs show only info-level GetCartAsync calls. That points to a connectivity or cart-side problem, not a checkout bug. Next I'll check whether cart's server spans appear in the same window, how long checkout's GetCart calls take, and whether checkout logs the dial error.

Checkout's failing GetCart client spans all dial cart:9999 (10.96.20.113) and hit i/o timeout, and no cart server spans for GetCart exist in the window, while cart logs only show info lines. Cart's own error traces show flagd connection refused (flagd:8013), which I haven't yet ruled in or out. Next I'll check flagd's error logs, cart's most recent logs and whether any error appears there, and open a second failing trace to confirm the cart span is missing.

Checkout's failing GetCart calls all dial cart at 10.96.20.113:9999 and hit i/o timeout, but no cart-side GetCart server spans appear in the window, and cart logs show only info lines. I need to know whether cart restarted or stopped listening, and when the failures started. Next I'll check cart's listening/startup logs over a longer window, look for earlier GetCart server spans, and find the onset of checkout's errors.

Checkout's failing spans all dial cart at 10.96.20.113:9999 and hit i/o timeout, and checkout's config points at cart:9999, so the address is correct. Cart shows no GetCart server spans in 60 minutes and no error logs, and its only startup log is from 19:12:32. Cart is the likely broken dependency, but the tools I have cannot show rollout history or Kubernetes events, so the cause within cart is not yet known. I am stopping here and handing off to the synthesizer.
Starting broad: checkout's rollout history, flag states across all flags, and recent warning events in the namespace. Then I'll diff any revision near the alert start and check the dependencies.

Checkout revision 2 landed at 19:23:33Z, about 2.5 minutes before the alert opened at 19:26:03, with the change-cause "cart client moved to port 9999". All 18 flags are off, so flags are not the cause. Next I'll diff checkout's revisions to see the exact change, check checkout's own events, and check cart's rollout to confirm whether cart is listening on the new port.

The checkout diff shows a single env change, CART_ADDR cart:8080 -> cart:9999, rolled out at 19:23:33Z, 2.5 minutes before the alert. Cart has only revision 1 from 19:11:23Z, so it was not changed. Next I'll check cart's events to see whether it is healthy and whether anything points to a port 9999 mismatch.

The only change near the alert is checkout revision 2 at 19:23:33Z, which changed CART_ADDR from cart:8080 to cart:9999, about 2.5 minutes before the alert. Cart has not changed since 19:11:23Z, and no warnings in the namespace point at checkout or its dependencies. I did not directly verify which port cart listens on, so the mechanism is an inference that the next step should confirm with cart client-span errors.

The investigators agree that checkout's GetCart calls to cart:9999 time out on dial, starting about 2.5 minutes after checkout revision 2 changed CART_ADDR from cart:8080 to cart:9999. Cart is unchanged and shows no server-side errors, so checkout's config is the most likely root cause, though cart's listening port has not been confirmed. result.report_summary: Checkout revision 2 (19:23:33Z, change-cause 'cart client moved to port 9999') is the only change before the alert (19:26:03Z). Its single diff is CART_ADDR cart:8080 -> cart:9999. Cart itself has not changed since 19:11:23Z, and flags are all off. The likely cause is checkout pointing at a wrong cart port, but I have not confirmed that cart listens only on 8080.

Checkout's failures trace to GetCart calls to cart:9999 (10.96.20.113) that time out on dial. Checkout logs no errors and only propagates the failure. Cart shows no GetCart server spans and no error logs in 60 minutes, which points to cart being unreachable or not serving, not to checkout. The cause within cart (pod, rollout, or network) is not determined by my data.

Checkout is the service failing: its server error ratio rose from about 0.18 to 0.54 between 19:24 and 19:27, and about 80% of its PlaceOrder spans are errors. The errors come from checkout's client calls to CartService/GetCart, but cart's own server spans show no errors and steady latency, so cart is not the origin. Frontend and frontend-proxy show only symptom-level error rates (about 0.03). The root cause inside checkout or its path to cart is not yet identified.

inferences.statement: The checkout config change to cart:9999 is the origin of the incident. Checkout is failing only on the cart path, and cart is healthy on its own side with no GetCart traffic arriving from checkout.
Checkout is a propagating symptom of the cart call failure, not an independent fault. Frontend and frontend-proxy errors (about 0.03) are downstream of checkout.

root_causes.cause: Revision 2 misconfigured CART_ADDR to cart:9999 (was cart:8080). Checkout's GetCart dials to port 9999 time out, so every PlaceOrder that needs the cart fails with Unavailable. The fix is to revert CART_ADDR to cart:8080 or roll back to revision 1.

diagnosis.summary: Checkout's error burn began about 2.5 minutes after checkout revision 2 (change-cause 'cart client moved to port 9999') was rolled out. That revision's only diff sets CART_ADDR from cart:8080 to cart:9999. Checkout's GetCart calls to 10.96.20.113:9999 time out on dial, and each one fails PlaceOrder. Cart is unchanged, has no server-side errors, and has no GetCart server spans in the last hour, so it is not receiving these calls. Most likely fix: point CART_ADDR back to cart:8080 (roll back checkout to revision 1), after confirming cart's listen port. Cart's listen port is not yet verified, and the metrics and log findings conflict on whether cart is serving any GetCart traffic.
